subtype: Approach: keeping a running record of achievements [Action]
passage:
Looking back, the thing that changed my review was a plain file. The year before, I could barely remember what I'd done between January and June. So on the last day of every month I started a note: what I delivered, numbers if I had them, and any kind words. March: the invoice report that saved the finance team forty hours. April: a thank-you line from Naveen, my manager, about the client demo. When review season came and Naveen asked, "What have you achieved this year?", I didn't have to search my memory. I scrolled through the note and read out six items. It took ten minutes and felt like a conversation about facts, not about how well I recalled the year. I still write it every month.

Maria

qa.q: How many items did Maria read out in the review?
How did Maria feel in the review after keeping the note?
qa.a: Maria felt calm and prepared, since there was no need to search memory.

qa.q: What else could Maria add to the note, and why?
qa.a: Maria could add a line on what was learned each month, because it shows growth as well as results.

qa.q: How might Naveen have found the review conversation?
qa.a: Naveen probably found it easier and clearer, since specific facts gave the discussion something solid to talk about.

grounding: Illustrates keeping a monthly note of delivered work, numbers and feedback so review conversations are concrete rather than memory based.
